title: Dispatch Telemetry Schema and Fallback Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document defines the canonical telemetry schema emitted at the dispatch layer, describes the signal->decision mapping used by the runtime to enact fallbacks, and provides an operational playbook for on-call and engineering teams to diagnose and remediate dispatch-induced degradations. The intent is to ensure consistent instrumentation, make fallback triggers auditable, and provide a reproducible validation and benchmarking process prior to rollout.

Scope
-----
Applies to: dispatch-svc (request router), kernel-orchestrator, runtime-admission-controller, and the observability pipelines that consume their telemetry.
Excludes: user-facing application logs, customer prompts, and post-hoc analysis performed by product analytics.

Why this matters
-----------------
- Dispatch is the first decision point that affects latency, model fidelity, and per-token cost.
- Inconsistent telemetry or opaque fallback decisions have caused missed SLAs and customer surprises in previous incidents.
- This playbook standardizes signals so automated escalation and incident playbooks can be deterministic.

Telemetry Schema (dispatch layer)
--------------------------------
Emit these fields on every request event (JSON schema example):

Example event (flattened JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-03T14:11:22Z",
  "req_id": "req_6a2f9b",
  "tenant_id": "team-alpha",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "model_variant": "rw-13b-quant-a",
  "dispatch_decision": "scheduled",  // scheduled | fallback | queued | rejected
  "kernel_id": "k-03",
  "kernel_queue_time_ms": 12.4,
  "kernel_exec_time_ms": 78.2,
  "end_to_end_latency_ms": 142.8,
  "token_count": 64,
  "cost_estimate_units": 0.024,
  "priority": "standard",
  "cohort": "mixed-burst",
  "prefetch_hit": false,
  "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.0,
  "fallback_reason": "kernel-unavailable", // optional string when dispatch_decision == fallback
  "decision_trace": ["slot-claim","kernel-hedge"],
  "sampling_score": 0.63
}

Signal catalog and semantic definitions
--------------------------------------
- dispatch_decision: high-level outcome of routing. Values and semantics in table below.
- kernel_queue_time_ms: time spent waiting in kernel dispatch queue (critical for tail latency).
- kernel_exec_time_ms: wall time of in-kernel execution. Excludes queue time
- end_to_end_latency_ms: total time from HTTP ingress to response commit
- prefetch_hit: whether a prefetcher predicted and warmed the KV cache for this session
- decision_trace: ordered list of decision checkpoints (useful for replay and audit)

Alerting thresholds and SLO mappings
-----------------------------------
We maintain per-tenant and global SLOs. The dispatch layer maps signal anomalies to alerts and automated fallbacks. Use the following baseline thresholds (table):

| Metric | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Action | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| p95 end_to_end_latency_ms (global) | 120 ms | 180 ms | Trigger latency-alert, cascade to autoscaler and runtime fallback policy | eng-sre |
| kernel_queue_time_ms (p99) | 50 ms | 150 ms | Increase priority for pinned kernels; enable hedging; if persists >5m -> fallback to compressed variant | runtime |
| dispatch_decision == rejected (rate) | 0.5% | 2% | Backpressure review; open incident if sustained >1m | eng-sre |
| fallback_rate (tenant, 1m) | 1% | 5% | Page product on degrading quality, run triage | runtime/product |
| kv_cache_hit_rate (cohort) | - | <10% sustained | Trigger KV cache warmup re-eval; run prefetcher audit | runtime |

Decision categories and recommended policies
-------------------------------------------
1) scheduled: proceed with selected kernel/model variant.
2) queued: admitted but awaiting slot. If queue exceeds 250ms (p95), enable short hedging to an opportunistic kernel.
3) fallback: routed to lower-cost or lower-fidelity variant to preserve latency SLO. Record fallback_reason.
4) rejected: admission controller refused due to quota or emergency backpressure. Return 429 with debug code.

Fallback decision matrix (example)
--------------------------------
If a decision point detects an anomaly, use tenant tier and request priority to calculate allowed fallback strategies.

- High priority (enterprise SLA): prefer region fallback before fidelity fallback.
- Standard: prefer fidelity fallback (quantized or distilled variant) before cross-region.
- Low: allow admission rejection if autoscaler capacity unavailable.

Matrix (simplified):

| Trigger | Enterprise | Standard | Low |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| kernel-unavailable | cross-region swap -> scheduled | model-quantized fallback -> scheduled | reject |
| kernel-thermal-throttle | migrate to warm node -> scheduled | model-quantized fallback -> scheduled | fallback -> reject if persists |
| sustained-high-queue | burst-scale slots + hedging | fidelity fallback + hedging | queue or reject |

Operational playbook (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------
The following steps assume an alert was raised for p99 kernel_queue_time_ms above critical for multiple kernels.

1) Triage (first 5 minutes)
  a) On-call reviews the alert, pulls the live dispatch dashboard (Dash: Dispatch/Kernel Queues).
  b) Check correlation between queue spike and recent deployments (check /releases and kernel-rollout feed).
  c) Inspect decision_trace sample stream for pattern (e.g., repeated "slot-claim-timeout").
2) Immediate mitigations (5--20 minutes)
  a) If spike is caused by a specific kernel_id and thermal/host issues: mark kernel node as drain-candidate and migrate sessions (CLI snippet below).
  b) Increase short-lived hedging for affected routes: set hedging multiplier to 2 for 10 minutes.
  c) Enable fidelity fallback for standard tenants: config change in runtime-admission-controller config map.
3) Root cause and resolution (>20 minutes)
  a) Capture representative traces (use sampling_score >0.5) and upload to incident artifact store.
  b) Run targeted microbenchmarks against kernel_id with synthetic corpus.
  c) If code regression suspected, roll back kernel/driver rollout per the kernel rollback playbook.
4) Post-incident
  a) Update incident report with timeline, decision_trace snippets, and corrective config changes.
  b) Propose adjustments to thresholds and fallback rules if behavior was expected under new traffic patterns.

Commands and examples
---------------------
Drain a kernel node (cli):

$ ri-runtimectl kernel drain --kernel-id k-03 --reason "thermal-throttle" --deadline 300s

Increase hedging for route (api):

POST /admin/runtime/hedging
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "multiplier": 2,
  "duration_s": 600
}

Patch admission controller to enable quantized fallback (kubectl patch example):

kubectl -n runtime patch configmap admission-config --patch '{"data":{"enable_quantized_fallback":"true"}}'

Benchmarks and validation before rollout
---------------------------------------
Before changing any dispatch decision logic or adding a new fallback path:
- Run the dispatch synthetic workload harness (see runbook: dispatch-synthetic-harness).
- Execute a fidelity-vs-latency sweep: quantify quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval metric) vs latency improvements for the candidate fallback.
- Validate end-to-end SLOs using the mixed-workload-slo-simulation suite with the same traffic signatures produced by our production traffic mirror.

Validation checklist (must pass all):
1) No more than 0.5% increase in error rate for enterprise tenants.
2) p95 latency improvement >= 10% in overloaded scenarios.
3) Rollback path tested in staging and rehearsal performed with chaos injection.

Observability and auditing
-------------------------
- Decision_trace must be retained for 30 days for all requests sampled with sampling_score > 0.5; store in compressed parquet in observability cluster.
- Fallbacks must emit a structured event (fallback_event) with metadata: {req_id, tenant_id, original_variant, fallback_variant, reason, latency_before, latency_after}.
- Maintain a daily fallback-rate report by tenant and route (automated job).

Ownership and contact list
--------------------------
- Dispatch service: runtime-dispatch@redwoodinternal (owner: Marcus Chen)
- Runtime admission controller: runtime-admission@redwoodinternal (owner: Priya Rao)
- Eng SRE on-call: see oncall roster

Rollout checklist (pre-deploy)
------------------------------
- [ ] Schema validated by telemetry team and CI schema checks pass.
- [ ] Synthetic harness pass at 10% and 100% load profiles.
- [ ] Canary rollout to 1% traffic for 4 hours with live metrics.
- [ ] Audit log retention and decision_trace retention configured.
- [ ] Runbook links and owner tags added to release notes.

Diagnostics tips and common failure modes
----------------------------------------
- Symptom: many fallbacks recorded with fallback_reason == "kernel-unavailable" but kernel hosts show healthy metrics.
  - Likely cause: admission-controller slot accounting mismatch. Check slot-claim timeout in decision_trace.
- Symptom: p95 latency improves after fallback but product quality complaints spike.
  - Action: revert fidelity fallback for affected tenant cohort and open product escalation.

Appendix: Lightweight schema registry (how to evolve)
---------------------------------------------------
1) Add new fields as optional and increment telemetry schema minor version.
2) Update CI schema-lint job to validate new fields against the registry.
3) Consumers must declare compatibility: any consumer that depends on a field must list it in the registry.
4) Deprecation policy: mark field deprecated for 60 days before removal; provide a migration adapter.

References
----------
- Execution contracts and stable fallbacks (see related pages)
- Kernel rollout and rollback playbook (kernel-and-scheduling)
- Mixed-workload SLO simulation suite (benchmarking-and-perf-suite)

If you find gaps or ambiguous signal semantics, open a PR against this page and ping the reviewers listed above.
